arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: the sides that brought the case argue federal funding recipients may be liable for compensatory damages.
They claim intentional conduct violates clear nondiscrimination statute terms.
the opposing sides argue the Rehabilitation Act and ACA differ from other statutes.
They state these laws contain no express causes of action for private remedies.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests whether federal funding recipients face liability for emotional distress damages. the sides that brought the case argue intentional discrimination triggers such liability. the opposing sides argue the statutes lack express causes of action. The Court must define the scope of available remedies.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This dispute defines the financial exposure of federal funding recipients. It clarifies the scope of compensatory damages for discrimination. The outcome shapes how states enforce nondiscrimination laws. It impacts the cost of compliance for healthcare providers. It determines the standard for emotional distress claims.
